name: p100
description: NVIDIA Tesla P100 PCIe (GP100, Pascal, sm_60) at its 1328 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 56 SMs (3584 CUDA cores), 64 resident warps per SM, 2 processing blocks each with its own warp scheduler and instruction buffer (NVIDIA Tesla P100 whitepaper)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GP100 SM processing block: 32 FP32 cores (FP32 and INT32), 16 FP64 cores, 8 LD/ST units and 8 SFUs (P100 whitepaper, Figure 8). One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block with the part's lanes. FP64 FMAs run on their own F64 FMA PEs (FMA64_PE_RATIO)
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: FP64 FMA at half the FP32 rate: 16 FP64 against 32 FP32 cores per processing block (P100 whitepaper; CUDA C++ Programming Guide, compute capability 6.0); 32 FPU lanes / 2
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 8 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, compute capability 6.0); 32 FPU lanes / 4
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM, 8 SFUs per processing block (P100 whitepaper)
sources.DCACHE_SIZE, DCACHE_NUM_WAYS: 24 KB unified L1/texture per SM (Jia et al., Table 3.1), separate from shared memory: 6 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE: 64 KB shared memory per SM (P100 whitepaper; CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 6.0)
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part. Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 4 MB L2 (P100 whitepaper; Jia et al., Table 3.1): 16 ways over power-of-two sets, 32 banks for the 32 memory channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 4 HBM2 stacks x 8 128-bit channels = 32 channels at 1430 MT/s: 32 x 16 B x 1430 MT/s = 732 GB/s (P100 whitepaper)
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_PEA: 1328 MHz maximum clock of the PCIe card, the clock Jia et al. measured at (Table 3.1); 732 GB/s
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE: Pascal has no tensor cores and no RT cores
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Off: the datacenter part is built for compute, so the profile models its compute machine, as a100 does
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: As in the other NVIDIA profiles: demand-paged MMU (introduced with Pascal), atomics with CAS, FP16, special-function units, 16 named barriers, texture units in every SM
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1: L1 hit 82 and L2 hit ~234 cycles on the P100. No DRAM latency is published, so dram_cycles is unchecked. Accel-Sim correlates this card (posted hardware runs: pascal-p100)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 27 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 82-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 61 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the 234-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Not set: no DRAM latency is published for this part, so dram_cycles is unchecked
